solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Company flying flag initially ran off at sea

parts.note: British Airways, a company that flies

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of 'flag'

explanation.surface: An airline with its flag flying has sailors deserting at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' sits at the end looking like part of the nautical scene; it is the definition, meaning confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at sea is bewildered, which is what baffled means.

clue.text: Perhaps Holly's outside watering hole, close to drunk

parts.note: a watering hole is a pub or bar

indicators.note: the close, or end, of 'drunk' is its last letter

explanation.surface: A woman called Holly is outside the pub, nearly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Holly reads as a woman's name, but it is the tree; its outside is its bark. 'Perhaps' flags holly as one example of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Bark is the outer layer of a tree such as holly.

clue.text: Particular, distasteful part of fish to start with

indicators.note: puts the fish part at the front

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish

explanation.surface: A fussy eater finds part of the fish distasteful for a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To start with' looks like a restaurant starter; it tells you which piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular person is fussy, which is finicky.

clue.text: Phone cases character used on Apple products overturned, making bloomer

indicators.note: turned upside down, which in a down entry reverses the letters

parts.note: the lowercase i of iPhone, iPad, iMac

explanation.surface: Phone cases printed with the Apple letter are turned over to reveal a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; here it is something that blooms, a flowering shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a shrub prized for its blooms.

clue.text: Tons invested in stock, flipping American junk

indicators.note: money invested in something goes into it

parts.note: a stock phrase is a tired one

explanation.surface: Tons of money put into shares, then flipping American junk bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' and 'invested' paint a stock market; stock here is the adjective, as in a stock phrase, meaning tired.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: detritus is debris, the worthless leftovers you would call junk.

clue.text: Dog collars cruciverbalists put back are delightful

definitions.note: the clue gives an adjective; BEWITCH is a verb, to delight

explanation.surface: Crossword fans find dog collars delightful when put back on.
explanation.walkthrough: Cruciverbalists are crossword solvers, so the setter counts you in. The definition is loose: the answer is a verb, and 'are delightful' must be read as 'delight'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym stretched across parts of speech: to bewitch is to enchant, which is to delight.

clue.text: Two pieces of personal info brought up in wine store

indicators.note: in a down entry, reads the pieces from the bottom up

parts.note: one piece of personal info: your age
the other: DOB, date of birth

explanation.surface: Personal details come up while shopping in an off-licence.
explanation.walkthrough: DOB is the standard form-filling abbreviation for date of birth. 'Brought up' works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or cellar.

clue.text: Funny writer with family penning poem

parts.note: a house is a family line, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: A humorist and his family write a poem together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' fits the writing picture but is the container instruction, not something the writer does.
explanation.definitionFit: P. G. Wodehouse, creator of Jeeves and Wooster, is one of the great comic writers.

clue.text: Tasteless stuff edging plain upholstery fabric

parts.note: tat is British slang for cheap, tasteless goods

explanation.surface: Cheap tasteless trimming along the edge of a plain sofa cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Tabaret is an obscure word, so the wordplay does the work here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabaret is a striped silk fabric used for upholstery.

clue.text: Cryptic indication of setter's part of town

parts.note: the answer, read as a clue in its own right, is wordplay whose result is the word setter
the definition: the main shopping street

explanation.surface: A question about which neighbourhood the setter lives in.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read HIGH STREET as wordplay, with high (drunk) as the anagram indicator and STREET the fodder, and it gives SETTER. The ’s is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The high street is the main shopping street of a British town.

clue.text: Fashion trend with gel covering one with curls

indicators.note: as a verb, to fashion is to shape anew
the rearranged letters cover the I

explanation.surface: A fashion trend for hair gel on someone with curls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' opens the clue looking like a noun beside trend; it is the verb telling you to rework TREND and GEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringleted hair is arranged in ringlets, long curls.

clue.text: Half-heartedly chattered about strip of clothing

indicators.note: turned about, facing the other way, so the letters reverse

parts.note: gabbed = chattered; losing one middle B leaves GABED

explanation.surface: Someone chatted half-heartedly about a strip of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip of clothing' looks like a scrap of fabric, but strip is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: debag is British slang meaning to strip someone of their trousers as a prank.

clue.text: Stick clutched by extremely cheeky tots in riding gear

indicators.note: takes the extremes, first and last letters, of cheeky

explanation.surface: Cheeky toddlers in riding kit clutch a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: Tots look like small children; they are measures of spirits, which the British call shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cycling shorts are what you wear to ride a bike.

clue.text: Recalling marines on strike, one could sound the reveille

parts.note: à la, in the manner of, recalling
to clock someone is to hit them

explanation.surface: Remembering marines who downed tools, one bugler could still sound the morning call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On strike' reads as industrial action, but strike is a verb meaning hit. À LA means 'in the style of', so a dish recalling another is à la it.
explanation.definitionFit: The reveille is the morning wake-up call, which is an alarm clock's job.

clue.text: Ruffian around a creek rolling over in lounger

indicators.note: something rolling over ends up the other way round

parts.note: a creek is a small bay or inlet

explanation.surface: A thug by a creek rolls over in his deckchair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounger' looks like a sunbed from the creek scene; it is a person who lounges about.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who lounges about idly is a layabout.

clue.text: Naughty dog, say, turned on kids' programme

indicators.note: a dog is one example of a pet

explanation.surface: A naughty dog turned on the children's TV.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue Peter is a long-running BBC children's TV show. 'Turned on' looks like switching on the set; it gives RE reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue Peter is a British children's television programme.

clue.text: Threaten to go out first from Gatwick Express

indicators.note: takes the first letter of Gatwick

explanation.surface: Travellers threaten a day out on the Gatwick Express, the London airport train.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gatwick Express is a train to the London airport, but it splits: Gatwick gives G and Express, a verb, gives UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle gutters when its flame flickers and threatens to go out.

clue.text: Affluent banks in Madrid bagging working capital

indicators.note: the banks of Madrid are its outer letters
to bag is to put in a bag

explanation.surface: Rich Spanish banks acquire working capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working capital' looks like a finance term; capital alone is the definition, a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Richmond is the capital of the US state of Virginia.

clue.text: Make good business, plugging pure rubbish

indicators.note: PURE is made rubbish of, jumbled

explanation.surface: A business makes good by selling pure rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make good' reads like making a profit; it is the definition, meaning make up a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to recoup losses is to recover them, making good what was lost.

clue.text: Comic actor's crack — brief piece of dialogue

indicators.note: cuts the last letter off line

explanation.surface: A comic actor's quip is one short line.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s means 'is'; crack looks like a wisecrack, but it is a split in the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin is the great silent-film comic actor.

clue.text: Perhaps someone shooting a bit of magic in EastEnders

indicators.note: the answer is a piece of the following words
the answer sits inside them

explanation.surface: A gunman brings a bit of magic to a British TV soap.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a British TV soap, and 'shooting' suits its gunplay; here it means filming.
explanation.definitionFit: A cineaste is a film enthusiast or film-maker, someone who might shoot a film.

clue.text: Thus accepting an outcome of sunbathing is very bad

explanation.surface: Getting a tan from sunbathing is very bad for you.
explanation.walkthrough: SIC is the Latin 'thus' used in quotations to flag an error as original.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means devilish, very bad indeed.

clue.text: Loaded son with possible reason for going to church

parts.words: possible reason for going to church

explanation.surface: A rich son has a possible reason for going to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' plays at being rich; it means packed away in a hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the shipping sense: goods stowed in a hold have been loaded aboard.

clue.text: Person holding cup? I bet that gets smashed — it's what impatient waiters do

indicators.note: I BET THAT is broken up and reassembled

parts.note: a champion holds the trophy cup

explanation.surface: A trophy winner is sure he'll get drunk while waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup' and 'smashed' suggest drinking; the cup is a trophy and waiters are simply people waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ at the bit is to be restless with impatience, like a horse chewing its bit.

clue.text: Barbarian aboard boat, regularly getting fare from Asia

indicators.note: takes every other letter of boat

explanation.surface: A barbarian on board a boat gets some Asian food.
explanation.walkthrough: Boat looks like the vessel the barbarian boards; only its alternate letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A bhuna is a dry, spicy curry from the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Wander off, ditching right guy

parts.note: to wander off is to stray

explanation.surface: Someone wanders off and dumps the right man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man; it is a rope bracing a mast or tent, which is also a stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay and a guy are both supporting ropes.

clue.text: Creature that flies round lake in rainy weather

explanation.surface: A bird flies round a lake in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one bird in flight, which is why the definition blends into the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: an owlet is a young owl, and a creature that flies is a vague way of saying bird.

clue.text: Doctor to unwind, absorbing hospital casebook?

indicators.note: as a verb, to doctor is to tamper with, so rearrange

explanation.surface: A doctor relaxes with a hospital case file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' and 'hospital' paint a medical scene, and doctor is the anagram indicator. The question mark flags casebook as a playful definition: a book about a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunnit is a detective story, literally a book about a case.

clue.text: Mellow wine, like certain spirits

explanation.surface: A mellow wine, like some spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Wine leads you to read spirits as drink; they are souls, as in kindred spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred spirits are like-minded people, so kindred is how certain spirits are described.

clue.text: Activity handymen do, maintaining cunning system with two rulers

explanation.surface: Handymen doing maintenance with a clever system of two rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maintaining' and 'rulers' fit the handyman scene, rulers as measuring sticks; here rulers are monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: From Greek: di- is two and -archy is rule, so a diarchy is rule shared by two.
